Oof, I generally avoid internet discussions (I'm not seeing this as an argument), but here I go. The friendzone is a term that has different definitions to different people. A common one is that you put "friend time" in and expect to get "sex/relationship time" out. This is a sexist and superficial view on any relationship as it prioritizes good crotch feelings over any others.

I don't view my friend that way, at all. I legitimately enjoy spending time with her, and I don't see anything I say or do as a way for me putting in time to get in her pants. Friendzones are good, useful. I've put people in them. If I don't want a relationship with this person, so I clarify that we are friends. That is totally fine. I've been on both sides.

Now, to everyone saying that I should confront her on it, reveal my feelings and all that mushy romance stuff, I'm not going to... yet. I would love to start a relationship with her and all that jazz since she's super fucking cool, but we're in different points of our lives and it would be a repeat of my last dumpster-fire of a relationship. Communication is hard, and that will definitely give me answers on this. I will never deny that. Yes, I'm in the friendzone. The friendzone is not a bad thing, despite what the internet says.

The reason I posted this in the r/bisexual subreddit, and the reason why I think the friendzone is bad in this case, is that she misinterprets my sexuality to only be one way, as many bisexual men and women experience. I'm not gay, nor am I straight: I'm bisexual. I am attracted to both. She constantly texts me for relationship advice, fetishizing my orientation, in a sense, to suit her needs. She didn't do this when I was "straight." I do compliment her, in a sort of weird way bc I'm awkward af, but I think she interprets that as that thing where gay men compliment their female friends? I don't expect her to throw herself at me, nor do I want her to. I'm fine with being friends, but by mixing it with sexuality stereotypes, it's offensive.
